translations.text: O Marbán, O hermit, why do you not sleep on a mattress? More often you used to sleep out in the open, with your head [?] on the floor of a pine wood.
I do not sleep on a mattress, though it might be [?] for my full health: there are many things outside [?] that [?] occupy my thoughts.
Our fellow pupils are not living; [?] parted from [?]: except for one person only, none of them is alive, O Guaire.
Ornat and full Lugna, Laidcenn and Ailerán, each of them devoted to his craft, Marbán and Cluithnechán.
You have heard my bequest, made at the time of my going from the world: my cup to the hermit, my sow to the sick Laidcenn.
My knife and my [?], my dwelling in Túaim Aidchi, my staff, my sow, my cup, my leather satchel, my [?].
O Marbán, O hermit, what has become of his bequest? [?] its blessing to the man of craft, except [?] its betrayal(?) to Mac Dúaid.
I have a hut in a wood; no one knows of it but my Lord. An ash tree on this side, a hazel on the other, a great tree of a ring-fort encloses it.
Two heather doorposts for support, and a lintel of honeysuckle. The wood around its edge sheds its mast on fat swine.
The size of my hut: small yet not small, a homestead of familiar paths. From its gable a she-bird in her blackbird-coloured cloak sings a sweet song.
The stags of Druim Rolach leap out of its very clear stream. From it can be seen red Roigne, noble Mucraime, and Máenmag.
A little hidden, [?] retreat that has [?] a well-trodden path. Will you come with me to see it? (I would pass my life without you.)
A mane of green-barked yew [?] (of the books [?]): it upholds the sky [?]! Lovely the place: the great green of an oak [?] beyond the charm [?].
An apple tree with apples (of great bounty), [?] abundant; a fine fistful cluster from a small-nutted, branching, green hazel.
Clear wells, waterfalls of water (excellent to drink) — they gush in abundance; yew berries, bird-cherry [?], privet [?].
Around it lie tame swine, goats, young pigs, wild swine, tall deer, does, a brood of badgers [?], badgers;
A peaceful band, a heavy host of the countryside, a gathering at my house; to its edge come foxes: that is lovely!
Fine feasts come (to my house [?]), a ready supply: pure water, [?] (everlasting [?]), salmon, trout.
Clusters of rowan berries, black sloes of the dark blackthorn, foods of [?] berries, bare berries (of bare slopes [?]).
A clutch of eggs, honey, mast, heath-pea [?] (God has sent it), sweet apples, red bog-berries, whortleberries.
Ale with herbs, a patch of strawberries, good to taste and of fine colour, [?] haws, berries of yew [?], kernels of nuts.
A cup of mead from the fine hazel [?], served swiftly; brown acorns, tangles of bramble with good blackberries.
And in summer, a pleasant coloured mantle, a delicious savour: pignuts [?], wild marjoram, green leeks [?], green clearness [?];
Music of the bright-breasted [?] birds, a beloved movement [?]; the humming of [?] thrushes, pleasant and familiar, above my house;
Bees, beetles, the round little craftsman [?], a gentle humming; wild geese, barnacle geese, shortly before Samain (1 November), the music of the rough dark one [?];
Lovely is the [?] (busy?) one, the brown [?] wren on the hazel branch; woodpeckers with their pied hoods on an oak, a vast throng.
Fair white ones come, herons and seagulls; the sea sings to them. No mournful music is that of the dun grouse from the russet heather.
The heifer lows (?) in summer, brightest of seasons: nothing bitter or toilsome over the soft, delightful, smooth plain.
The sound of the wind against the branching wood, a grey cloud; the river's waterfalls; the swan's cry: lovely music.
Beautiful are the pines that make music for me, and I did not hire them. Through Christ, I am no worse off at any time than you are.
Though you delight in what you enjoy, greater than any wealth, I am thankful for what is given to me by my gentle Christ.
Without an hour of strife, without the din of quarrelling that troubles you, I am thankful to the Prince who gives me every good thing in my hut.
I would give my glorious kingship, together with my share of Colmán's inheritance, to be mine until the hour of my death, to be in your company, Marbán.
